invariants.statement: A pending manifest makes the first user interaction a focused Project Definition Intake; Codex challenges material ambiguity, gives a final correction opportunity, records only user-confirmed durable truth, and the same focused intake resumes later when a material decision changes.

Local Codex memory isolation is repository-local and root-bound under ignored `.codex/runtime/`; generated projects receive no framework or sibling runtime or memory state and use memories only inside their own clean runtime home.

Root `src/` is the default Product Root; non-trivial product code starts as a modular monolith with cohesive replaceable components or modules, narrow public contracts, private internals, owned data and migrations, and explicit acyclic dependencies. Components must remain independently improvable or replaceable while their contracts, data semantics, lifecycle, and failure behavior stay compatible and the assembled system is verified as one functioning unit.

Central `main` is the only durable integration branch; a serialized writer uses it directly only when branch policy permits, different developers use temporary task branches, parallel writers use disjoint scopes and one write owner per module or shared surface, same-account worktrees are not an authentication boundary, and shared-contract work has one integrator. Before every slice begins and before any expanded write scope, perform a pre-slice coordination check based on the current goal, slice, modules, contracts, data surfaces, and repository-relative write set: inspect all observable agent, session, account, and team-channel claims before relying on Git, permit only confirmed-disjoint parallel work, and resolve overlap or uncertain shared ownership to exactly one writer before writing. A local runtime lease or quiet worktree cannot prove that another clone, machine, or account is idle; use a shared coordination channel across that boundary and fail closed on uncertain shared ownership.

Every new feature and complex task uses reviewable slices; every completed slice repeats focused verification and review/repair until no relevant finding remains, then receives a fresh audit and whole-repository course check, any audit finding reopens the loop, and the course check repeats at each major milestone. When research or publications inform work, search for and prioritize the newest relevant primary or official sources, verify publication or update date, version, correction or retraction state, and applicability, distinguish evidence from inference, and use older sources primarily for comparison or historical context; rely on an older foundational or controlling source as current authority only with an explicit reason and verification that newer evidence has not superseded it. At every completed goal, before the final audit and publication, perform an all-document currency review of all active documentation against current behavior and durable truth; update only where needed, consolidate or remove obsolete and duplicate material instead of appending history, and preserve every active directive. Consolidation is not a shortening target. Treat the durable project manifest as critical documentation; inspect it and every other critical authority read-only first, change them automatically only when the factual correction and full preservation are unambiguous, otherwise obtain explicit user confirmation before writing, and give every authorized critical-document change a separate preservation review.

Never end at "ready to implement" when implementation is already authorized. Plans, research, recaps, gates, reviews, audits, and readiness statements are intermediate. An authorized outcome spanning multiple goals or sessions keeps a bounded `docs/project-context.md` `codexrig-work-state` marker; only a durable local Stop event with a non-null `transcript_path` may reopen active work. Ephemeral side conversations and other transcriptless contexts exit before work-state or index access, while `stop_hook_active` plus private per-session state lets an unchanged already-continued durable turn stop instead of looping and a changed revision continue again. Failed publication leaves the current goal open, and published goals advance with `pnpm goal:new` without waiting for another prompt until the outcome or a real blocker is reached.

GitHub and GitLab keep equivalent portable CI, protected review and green-CI intent, provider-owned API configuration, and read-back verification; GitHub merge queues and GitLab merge trains provide equivalent merge serialization.

`.codexrig/framework.json` and `.codexrig/` own versioned compatibility, startup, provider, and upgrade policy; `pnpm framework:doctor -- --online` diagnoses health, only a reviewed, trusted CodexRig checkout may be applied, and transactional upgrades preserve unrelated local changes.
